lesson.title: Random Whole Numbers
lesson.driving_question: How can a program generate a whole number whose outcome varies within known limits?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Generating reproducible random whole numbers within inclusive bounds
lesson.concept_budget: Use a seed to make prediction deterministic and randint() for inclusive whole-number bounds; other random operations are deferred.
misconceptions: A fixed seed makes a sequence repeatable for investigation.
The generated value is stored before it is displayed.
Removing the seed after investigation restores varied runs.
lesson.progression_note: Introduces the Grade 7 random strand with deterministic classroom prediction before adding stepped ranges and choices.
code_expectations: fixed seed in the shared program

shared_program.code:
import random
random.seed(7)
roll = random.randint(1, 6)
print("Dice roll:", roll)

primm.prompt: Recall how a function receives arguments inside parentheses and how inclusive limits differ from a range() stop value.
The seed is fixed at 7. Predict the allowed values, then record the exact roll you expect before running the supplied file.
Run the unchanged file twice. Confirm that the fixed seed produces the same roll, then remove the seed line and compare several runs.

questions: Why can random.randint(1, 6) produce both 1 and 6?
What value is stored in roll when the starter program uses seed 7, and why does the same value appear on another run?
Why is the random result stored in roll before it is printed instead of calling randint() again in print()?

primm.prompt: Turn the die into a twelve-sided die. Keep seed 7; the displayed result must stay between 1 and 12 inclusive.
Generate two six-sided rolls, store each roll in a separate variable, and display their total. Keep seed 7.
Create a random practice target. Ask for a minimum and maximum whole number, generate one target inside those inclusive bounds, and display it with a label. Test bounds 4 and 4; the target must be 4.
Repair the module name, the missing comma and the misspelled result variable.
